acceptance_criteria: weekly-review.sh writes docs/weekly/YYYY-Www.md and leaves a plan marker
report flags verification-command paths that no longer exist
every completed feature's verification command resolves to existing paths
scripts/tests/test_weekly_review.sh passes and all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Added scripts/weekly-review.sh and scripts/tests/test_weekly_review.sh (9/9). First weekly review (2026-W41) found feat-058 verification pointed at renamed tests/test_ratchet_loop.py; fixed to test_ratchet_loop_runner.py and added the path check so it cannot recur silently. features.name: Multi-Agent Team Topologies, Hierarchical Supervisor, and Consensus Voting (Lecture 15)
features.description: Port Lecture 15 Multi-Agent Team Topologies, implementing hierarchical supervisor delegation, dynamic worker pools with isolated contexts, consensus voting engine (majority quorum, security veto), and production scripts/team_runner.py with full test verification.
acceptance_criteria: docs/harness-creator/lecture-15/ contains summary.md, progress-detail.md, and code/team_topology.md
docs/harness-creator/lecture-15/code/team_engine.py implements zero-dependency team orchestrator with Supervisor, WorkerPool, and ConsensusEngine
scripts/team_runner.py and scripts/team-runner.sh provide CLI multi-agent team runner
tests/test_team_runner.py and scripts/tests/test_team_runner.sh pass 100%
All fast tests and 11 harness gates pass cleanly
features.evidence: Authored Lecture 15 study materials under docs/harness-creator/lecture-15/ (summary.md, progress-detail.md, code/team_topology.md). Implemented zero-dependency Multi-Agent Team and Consensus engine in docs/harness-creator/lecture-15/code/team_engine.py with Supervisor, WorkerPool (timeout budget checking, isolated execution, non-dict wrapping), and ConsensusEngine (majority, unanimous, and security veto quorum rules with defensive reviewer exception handling). Promoted to production CLI runner in scripts/team_runner.py and scripts/team-runner.sh. Added automated unit tests in test_team_engine.py (14/14 passed) and tests/test_team_runner.py (3/3 passed), plus shell tests in scripts/tests/test_team_runner.sh (5/5 passed across macOS system Python 3.9 and Python 3.14). Independently audited by adversarial subagent; remediated all conditional findings (reconciled topology diagram, preserved NO_QUORUM status, hardened reviewer exception handling, enforced timeout budget). All fast tests (90/90) and 11 harness gates pass cleanly.

features.evidence: Added scripts/state_layer_check.py; the guard now calls it and maps any non-zero status to exit 2. Independent review (fresh-context subagent plus codex-kiro) found the guard exited 1 or 127 when the checker crashed or python3 was missing, which does not block; fixed with tests, and a self-referential trace_row test now asserts literal values. test_state_layer_guard.sh 44/44 on bash 5 and /bin/bash 3.2, test_session_clean.sh 8/8, tests/test_trace_evaluation.py 7/7. Converted 9 AGENTS.md and 6 lecture-doc file:/// links to relative paths. Dropped the redundant Write() deny rule in .claude/settings.json because Claude Code only consults Edit(path) rules.

features.name: Run telemetry: read-only collector, comparison report, outside-agent attempt log
features.description: Measure token use, duration, subagents and gate results per run from Claude Code session files without relying on the agent's own estimates, keep detail outside the state layer, and record every outside-agent attempt.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/run_telemetry.py deduplicates usage by (scope, message id), flags conflicting rows, never reports an unavailable metric as 0, and keeps parent and subagent usage separate
scripts/run_report.py prints missing metrics as n/a and compares runs in one table
cmd_run records every outside-agent attempt (including failures, timeouts, skips, interruptions) without changing return codes or candidate order
state layer stays within its 6,000-token budget and all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Collector, report and 53 tests (tests/test_run_telemetry.py, tests/test_run_report.py); 24 baseline records in docs/telemetry/runs/ from 22 existing sessions, with docs/telemetry/RELIABILITY.md listing each metric as measured, ambiguous or missing. Reviews: a fresh subagent and codex-kiro on the first draft found 12 defects (synthetic rows reported a context size of 0 in 4 sessions, 4 nested workflow subagents never read, crashes on non-hashable ids and NaN durations, committed records carrying agent type and session id verbatim, window boundary rows counted twice); each got a failing test first and a fix. Attempt logging for outside_agent.py got a subagent and codex-kiro review; the SIGTERM path was found by both and fixed. Not done: USD cost (no authoritative source), outcome and retries (no structured record), Codex/Kiro/agy token usage (none usable), and running the fixed benchmark defined in docs/stories/run-telemetry/benchmark.md.
features.verification: bash scripts/harness-verify.sh && python3 -m pytest tests/test_run_telemetry.py tests/test_run_report.py tests/test_outside_agent.py -q

features.name: Fixed telemetry benchmark: five tasks, scripted checks, runner and comparison
features.description: Answer whether a harness change made the next task of the same difficulty faster, cheaper or more reliable, using fixed prompts, frozen fixtures, hidden checks and no model-based scoring.
acceptance_criteria: each of B1-B5 has a frozen prompt, a fixture, and scripted checks that fail on the untouched fixture and pass on a reference solution
compare prints no verdict with fewer than 5 runs per version, and only between runs that share model and suite hash
a run's telemetry counts only that run's outside-agent attempts
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: scripts/telemetry_benchmark.py, benchmarks/telemetry/ (suite, fixtures, hidden tests, reference solutions; python files stored as *.fixture so mypy and the bash guard skip them), tests/test_telemetry_benchmark.py (38 tests, fake agent, no tokens). One real run of each task on claude-sonnet-5.5 passed. Two defects found by the smoke runs (B2 check rejected a legitimate added test; run telemetry counted the global outside-agent log) and 8 more by a fresh subagent plus codex-kiro (hidden dir exposed via BENCH_DIR, first-pass compared as a point, missing subagents read as 0, harness commit turned -dirty by its own output, missing agent binary crashed the batch, B1 accepted a hard-coded answer, B3 matched negated sentences, B5 only checked that ids survived); each got a failing test first. Not done: the 5-runs-per-version comparison itself (about 50 sessions, run it when a harness change needs measuring), gate results per task (fixture repos have no gates), a second harness version to compare against. B3 scoring is keyword-based and can misjudge unusual phrasing.

features.name: Faster gates and automatic run records: parallel tests, process adherence, feature summaries, review timeout
features.description: Cut the verify time, make every task leave its own telemetry without manual steps, and make outside-agent failures explain themselves.
acceptance_criteria: run-tests.sh runs files in parallel and prints the same lines, order, counts and exit code as the sequential run; a killed test is a failure; a signal stops the queue
every run record carries process_adherence (hook feedback, review attempts by family, subagents by type) with unmeasurable rules marked missing

session-clean attaches a summary to each completed feature, archives old features to keep the state layer under 6000 tokens without losing any, and keeps the last gate report for the window it falls in
outside-agent reviews default to 300 s and failed attempts log a bounded, scrubbed reason; return codes, order and classification are unchanged
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Full gate time fell from about 220 s to 75-85 s (tests gate 70 s); 93 test files, identical ordered output at 1 and 4 jobs, 12 jobs x5 stress, SIGINT/SIGTERM leave no process. process_adherence measured on 76 real sessions with no change to existing fields. feature_run_record.py: 30 tests, 3,324 budget cases with no loss and none left over budget. outside_agent.py: 131 tests. Reviews by a fresh subagent, codex-kiro and agy found about 30 defects across the rounds (lost features without an id, archive overwrite and path escape, kill diagnostics interleaving, --jobs swallowing a flag, orphaned queue after SIGTERM, credential-shaped guard names, unscrubbed error text); each got a failing test first. Not done: gate-necessity experiment, the 5-runs-per-version benchmark comparison, SubagentStop double counting is unverified, claude-kiro is not an independent reviewer for a Claude caller by design.
